title: Day-Zero experiment ops playbook (working)
body:
Purpose:
Quick operational handbook to run the first 72 hours of a cross-functional experiment or canary ("day-zero" meaning the go-live window and immediate stabilization). This is intentionally terse — a checklist + signal matrix + communication templates engineers, product, SRE, and CS can use when kicking off a new route/variant/model.

Audience:
- Release steward (owner)
- Oncall SRE / telemetry engineer
- Product PM / Experiment lead
- Solutions / Support rep on rotation

High-level objectives:
- Get the experiment running with minimal blast radius
- Ensure early detection of regression and clear rollback criteria
- Make decisions fast: who calls rollback, who triages, who talks to customers

Scope & when to use:
- Suitable for: model variant A/B, routing change, new latency-sensitive feature, algorithmic ranking change.
- Not for: full infra upgrades (use infra release playbook), security patches.

Day-zero quick checklist (minimum viable):
1) Ownership: assign steward + contactable oncall for first 72 hours. (steward = PM or Eng lead).
2) Traffic partition: start <= 1% for 0–30m, step to 5% after 30–90m if green, then 15% after 3–6h. Adjust to product risk.
3) Fallback ready: pre-provisioned route back to baseline model pinned with same input schema. Test the fallthrough locally.
4) Alerting: ensure alerts (pager/Slack) exist for the signal matrix below and that escalation tags point to steward + SRE.
5) Synthetic traffic: run canonical prompt set through experiment route (smoke + latency + failure-inject patterns).
6) Observability wireup: confirm dashboards are live and sampling traces are capturing variant tags.
7) Cost guardrail: if per-token cost > 2x baseline for 10m, trigger autoscale to baseline and notify finance-ops.
8) Customer notice: if experiment touches known enterprise customers, pre-notify CS and list mitigation steps.
9) Throttle knobs: verify feature flag + kill-switch + traffic weight API are all functional.
10) Communication template ready in Slack and email.

Signal matrix (early-warning signals, prioritized):
- Severity A (immediate pager; immediate rollback candidate)
  - Error rate (5xx or 4xx of new route) > 1% absolute and 3x baseline for 5m
  - Latency p99 > baseline p99 + 400ms for 5m
  - Token generation anomalies: exponential output length or recurrent diverging tokens (heuristic via evals)
- Severity B (paged to steward, triage within 15m)
  - Quality regressions on daily prompt set: drop in eval score > 7% compared to baseline
  - Increased downstream user retries > 2x baseline for 10m
- Severity C (on dashboard, notify)
  - Cost-per-request trending up > 25% for 30m
  - Small uptick in non-critical errors or rare edge-case responses seen in sampling

Decision ladder / who calls what:
- Automated actions: kill-switch executes immediate rollback if Severity A alert is triggered twice in a rolling 10m window.
- Human actions: steward + oncall confer within 5m of first Severity A. If unresolved in 10m, steward escalates to SRE lead to approve rollback.
- Customer-impacting: if enterprise customer latency/error exceeds SLO, CS lead drafts immediate outreach; steward decides whether to isolate that customer route.

Observability checklist (concrete):
- Dashboards: traffic split by cohort, p50/p95/p99 latency by route, error rate by route, cost per 1k tokens by route.
- Traces: ensure request traces carry "experiment_id" and "variant" tags; sampling rate >= 5% for 1st 6h.
- Logs: make sure request/response examples are sharded to a secure bucket (PII redaction on).
- Evals: automated nightly evals on canonical prompt set + guard prompts (toxicity, hallucination).

Synthetic test matrix (pre-launch smoke):
- Smoke 1: baseline queries (100 reqs) for basic functionality OK
- Smoke 2: latency flood (simulate burst of 200 reqs/s for 2m), observe queuing/backpressure
- Smoke 3: fault-inject path (drop one GPU node) — ensure fallback automatically drains in 30s
- Smoke 4: edge-case prompt set (50 prompts flagged in prior experiments) — check for hallucination patterns

Fallback & rollback playbook (fast lane):
- Immediate rollback steps (sub-5m):
  1) Hit kill-switch in console (or feature flag rollback API)
  2) Route traffic to pinned baseline. Confirm via observability that traffic change completed.
  3) Post-rollback communication to Slack release channel + broader stakeholders with timestamp + reason.
  4) Short incident note (link to ticket).
- Post-rollback: capture top 3 telemetry traces causing alert, tag on PR and block re-deploy until postmortem.

Communications templates (copy/paste):
- Slack (first alert): "[Canary] {steward} detected elevated {metric} on {variant}. Applying mitigation: pausing rollout to 0% and triaging. Pager: @{oncall}. More in {ticket_url}."
- Internal status update (30m): short bullets: what happened, mitigation, current traffic, next step, owners.
- Customer-facing: brief, empathetic, action-focused — CS will own message.

Operational run rules (social contract):
- No silent rollbacks: any rollback must be logged with short rationale and shared with cross-functional channel.
- No stealth exposure increases: steward must approve any >10% increment after 6h.
- Leave breadcrumbs: every change must have a linked ticket/PR and one-line rollout rationale.

Post-launch evaluation (by 72h):
- Run full eval suite vs baseline across quality, latency, cost.
- Straw poll with small set of product/stewards for subjective UX regressions.
- Decide: scale to GA (yes/no/iterate). If iterate, list hypothesis and experiments.

Quick templates for instrumentation changes (ops note):
- Add metric: name, unit, route tag (experiment_id), expected baseline, alert threshold. Keep metric cardinality low.
- Tracing: add variant tag as top-level span attribute; do not increase trace size >10KB.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Should we centralize synthetic traffic harness in Console or keep as repo scripts? (tradeoffs: reproducibility vs agility)
- Fine-tune the severity thresholds for small, high-volume endpoints (different baseline noise).
- Flesh out cost-guard rail rules with Finance — current threshold is a placeholder.
- Automate initial step-up schedule per product category (UI, reranker, embedding).

Appendix: quick links + helpers
- Quick rollback API snippet (curl) — saved in internal snippets repo (link in linked_artifacts)
- Short checklists for SRE oncall (copy to rotation playbook)

Notes (informal):
- Keep this doc intentionally minimal — teams should copy and adapt rather than request changes here.
- Will convert to templates in Console (release wizard) once patterns are stable.

Last updated notes:
- 2026-03-01: tightened latency p99 threshold language and added cost guardrail note (Maya).
- 2025-11-10: initial draft and field-tested on two small reranker canaries (Owen, Priya).

Unresolved: who owns synthetic prompt canonicalization (prod vs applied-ml) — flag for next sync.
